n101.text: Last time, we made an electromagnet by the electrical method. Take the battery away, and the clips drop off.

n202.text: A little cricket is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

n204.text: Lock in first with your fingers. One finger for every point.

n401.text: Round one. Momo's nail has ten turns of wire, and Basil's has twenty. Each has one battery. Which nail attracts more steel clips? One, ten turns. Two, twenty turns. Three, both the same. Show me your fingers.

n403p.text: Three. They both have one battery, and only batteries make an electromagnet stronger.

n404b.text: Two! More turns is like more strokes. More turns, more pull!

n405m.text: Two. Every turn of wire helps a little, so twenty turns help more.

n501.text: Be a steel bolt! Shrink down. Quietly.

n502.text: You are a steel bolt in our mini scrapyard, the heaviest scrap of all. Aluminium ring-pulls and plastic caps lie around you.

n503.text: Momo's hook with ten turns comes down. You tip up a little, and then you slip back down.

n504.text: Here comes Basil's hook with twenty turns. You jump up, and cling to its tip! The ring-pulls stay behind.

n601.text: The answer is two: Basil's twenty turns! Did you show two fingers? Put one finger up!

n602b.text: A turn of wire is one time the wire goes round the nail, such as the twenty turns round my nail!

n701p.text: But it is the same battery. How can more turns make it stronger?

n702.text: Look closer. The same nails, the same wire, and one battery each. Only the number of turns is different.

n703.text: The nail with twenty turns attracts more steel clips. Each turn of wire adds a little more pull.

n704m.text: The strength of an electromagnet is how strongly it pulls, such as how many steel clips it can attract!

n705.text: Our school bell has an electromagnet inside, with many turns of wire. It switches on and off very fast, so a little hammer hits the bell again and again!

n707.text: We can increase the strength of an electromagnet by increasing the number of turns of wire around the iron nail.

n801.text: Showdown! Double points. Momo's poster for Recycling Week has one mistake. Line one, two, or three? Show me with your fingers.

n802m.text: One: coil a long wire round the iron nail. Two: join both ends to the battery. Three: electricity is stronger, so a light wooden chopstick works too!

n804b.text: Three! A wooden chopstick cannot be made into a magnet, even with electricity. Wood is not a magnetic material.

n805.text: Three fingers? Put up two more on your score hand!

n806s.text: Objects made of iron and steel can be made into magnets using the stroke method or the electrical method.

n901b.text: We have used up all our wire. How else can we make our crane stronger?

n902.text: Look closer. Two nails, each with twenty turns. One is joined to one battery. The other is joined to two batteries, in a row.

n903.text: The nail with two batteries attracts more steel clips. More batteries make more electricity flow round the coil.

n904p.text: The number of batteries is how many batteries we join together, such as one battery, or two batteries in a row!

n905.text: Watch! Our crane carries the steel bolt to the lorry, and drops it in!

n907.text: We can also increase the strength of an electromagnet by increasing the number of batteries used.

c1003.text: More turns of wire? A stronger electromagnet! More batteries? A stronger electromagnet! The wall socket? Never! Batteries only!

n1101.text: Show me your score hand! Two fingers or more? You beat the Buddies. Three fingers? High five!

n1102.text: Did you spot the cricket? It was on the ledge, right under the school bell!

n1103m.text: Here is a fun fact! A cricket's ears are on its front legs, just below its knees! So when our school bell rings, the cricket hears it with its legs!

n1201.text: Next time: Basil tests which makes a stronger electromagnet, an iron nail or a steel nail. He coils twenty-five turns round the iron nail, but only eight turns round the steel nail. Is his test fair? One, yes. Two, no. Lock in your answer!

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?
